prompt: The spec says "users can reset passwords", and reviewers argue about whether expired links and rate limits were in scope.
tells: argue about whether expired links and rate limits
why: Add checkable criteria: given an expired link, when clicked, then show X.
trap: Non-goals rule things out; criteria define done.

prompt: Each requirement is written as "given a cart over $50, when the user checks out, then shipping is free".
why: That's the given/when/then form of acceptance criteria.
trap: They can become tests, but they're criteria first.

prompt: The agent handled the happy path but not empty carts, coupons or out-of-stock items, none of which the spec mentioned.
tells: none of which the spec mentioned
why: List edge cases as acceptance criteria so they're part of done.
trap: The agent can't satisfy conditions nobody wrote down.

prompt: A requirement says the page "should load fast". The agent says it's done; users disagree.
why: Make it measurable: "under 1.5 s p75 on a mid-range phone".
trap: Verification needs something checkable to verify.
